Rashi on Eruvin 61b:11:1.hebrew: הדר עם העכו"ם או עם מי שאינו מודה בעירוב - כותי, כדאמר בפרק בכל מערבין (עירובין דף לא:):
Rashi on Eruvin 61b:11:1.english: One who resides with an idolater, or with one who does not accept the eiruv - [This refers to] a Samaritan, as [the Gemara] said in the chapter [entitled] Bekhol Me'arvin (Eruvin 31b):

Rashi on Eruvin 61b:11:2.hebrew: אוסר עליו - לטלטל מביתו לחצר, עד שישכור הימנו רשות שיש לו בחצר:
Rashi on Eruvin 61b:11:2.english: Renders it prohibited for him - To carry from his house into the courtyard, until he rents from him the rights that he has in the courtyard.

Rashi on Eruvin 61b:12:1.hebrew: עד שיהו ב' ישראלים - דרין בב' בתים, ואוסרין זה על זה, ובאין לערב ביניהן — הנכרי אוסר עליהן, אבל על היחיד אינו אוסר. ובגמרא מפרש טעמא:
Rashi on Eruvin 61b:12:1.english: Unless there are two Jews - Who dwell in two houses and prohibit one another, and come to make an eiruv between them — the gentile renders it prohibited for them, but for an individual, he does not render it prohibited. And in the Gemara, the reason is explained.

Rashi on Eruvin 61b:13:1.hebrew: מעשה בצדוקי אחד - קסבר ר"ג: צדוקי אינו כעכו"ם, ולא דמי לכותי — דגרי אריות הן ואינם גרים גמורים; אבל צדוקי — ישראל הוא ונהפך למינות, ואינו מודה בתורה שבעל פה. כיון דישראל הוא, יכול לבטל רשותו בלא שום שכירות:
Rashi on Eruvin 61b:13:1.english: An incident involving a certain Sadducee - Rabban Gamliel maintains: A Sadducee is not like an idolater, nor is he similar to a Samaritan — for they are lion-converts and are not full converts. But a Sadducee is an Israelite who turned to heresy, and does not accept the Oral Torah. Since he is an Israelite, he can renounce his domain without any rental.

Rashi on Eruvin 61b:13:2.english: An incident involving a Sadducee who lived with us in an alleyway - And he renounced his domain to us.

Rashi on Eruvin 61b:13:3.hebrew: ואמר לנו אבא מהרו והוציאו כליכם למבוי - והחזיקו בו כיון דקדש היום מיד, כדי שלא יחזור בו:
Rashi on Eruvin 61b:13:3.english: And Father said to us: Hurry and take out your utensils to the alleyway - And establish possession of it immediately once the day has become sanctified, so that he does not retract [his renunciation].

Rashi on Eruvin 61b:13:4.hebrew: עד שלא יוציא - כליו תחילה, ויחזור ויחזיק ברשותו, ויאסור עליכם. וש"מ דאינו כנכרי, דאי אגירו מיניה, היכי מצי למהדר? אע"ג דמפיק, לא אסר, דהא נקיט דמי:
Rashi on Eruvin 61b:13:4.english: Before he takes out - His utensils first, and retract and repossess his domain, and prohibit [it] to you. And learn from this that he is not like a gentile; for if they had rented [it] from him, how could he retract? Even though he takes [utensils] out, he does not prohibit [it], for behold, he has accepted payment.

Rashi on Eruvin 61b:14:1.hebrew: מהרו ועשו צרכיכם במבוי - מבעוד יום, דבשבת לא מהני לכו האי ביטול שמא יוציא ויאסור עליכם. דקסבר רבי יהודה: אע"ג דהחזיקו בני מבוי במבוי תחילה — מצי לאהדורי ביה:
Rashi on Eruvin 61b:14:1.english: Hurry and do your needs in the alleyway - While it is still day, for on Shabbat this renunciation will not avail you, lest he take out [utensils] and render [the alleyway] prohibited for you. For Rabbi Yehuda holds: Even though the residents of the alleyway took possession of the alleyway first, he can retract [his renunciation].

Rashi on Eruvin 61b:1:1.hebrew: בעיר חריבה - מדיוריה, אבל מחיצותיה קיימות סביב לה:
Rashi on Eruvin 61b:1:1.english: In a desolate city - [Desolate] of its inhabitants, but its partitions stand around it:

Rashi on Eruvin 61b:1:2.hebrew: לרבנן מהלך את כולה - דהא שבת באויר מחיצות, והוא הדין לר"ע. והא דנקט רבנן — משום המניח עירובו, דבעי למיתני חילוק בין חריבה לישיבה, ולר"ע אפי' בישיבה אין לו ממקום עירובו אלא אלפים:
Rashi on Eruvin 61b:1:2.english: According to the Rabbis he may walk through all of it - For he established his Shabbat residence within the airspace of partitions, and the same applies according to Rabbi Akiva. And that which [Shmuel] stated "according to the Rabbis" [is] on account of [the case of] one who placed his eiruv, where he wished to teach a distinction between a desolate [city] and an inhabited [one]; whereas according to Rabbi Akiva, even in an inhabited [city], he has only two thousand [cubits] from the place of his eiruv.

Rashi on Eruvin 61b:1:3.hebrew: הניח עירובו בעיר חריבה כו' - דכי אמור רבנן כל העיר לו כד' אמות — במיושבת, כדתנן בהדיא: ״אימתי? בזמן שאין בה דיורין״, אלמא בחריבה מודו:
Rashi on Eruvin 61b:1:3.english: [If] he placed his eiruv in a desolate city, etc. - For when the Rabbis said [that] the entire city is to him like four cubits, [it was only] in an inhabited [city], as we learned explicitly [in the Mishnah]: “When [does this apply]? When it has no residents”; thus, regarding a desolate [city], they concede [to Rabbi Akiva].

Rashi on Eruvin 61b:2:1.hebrew: ה"ג - הא באין בה דיורין מודין ליה:
Rashi on Eruvin 61b:2:1.english: This is the reading - Consequently, when it has no residents, they concede to him.

Rashi on Eruvin 61b:3:1.english: It is not fit for residence - That its walls have fallen.

Rashi on Eruvin 61b:4:1.hebrew: מערת צדקיהו - גדולה היתה, והיא שיצא בה צדקיהו לילה מירושלים לברוח מפני הכשדים, כדכתיב בירמיה (נב): "ותבקע העיר וגו'":
Rashi on Eruvin 61b:4:1.english: The Cave of Zedekiah - It was large, and it is [the cave] through which Zedekiah went out by night from Jerusalem to flee from the Chaldeans, as it is written in Jeremiah (52): "And the city was breached, etc."

Rashi on Eruvin 61b:4:2.hebrew: אף עיר חריבה - ועל כרחך חריבה מדיורין, ולא מחומה — דאי מחומה, לא הוי תני מהלך את כולה, כיון דלא שבת באויר מחיצות (וה"ה ר' עקיבא). ואע"ג דיש חומה — קתני שבת, ולא קתני הניח:
Rashi on Eruvin 61b:4:2.english: So too the city is desolate - And perforce, [it means] desolate of residents, and not [desolate] of a wall — for if [it were desolate] of a wall, [the baraita] would not have taught: “He may walk through all of it,” since he did not establish his Shabbat residence within the airspace of partitions (and the same applies according to Rabbi Akiva). And even though it has a wall, [the baraita] taught: “He established his Shabbat residence,” and did not teach: “He placed [his eiruv].”

Rashi on Eruvin 61b:5:1.english: Whose [opinion is this] - [Regarding] this [baraita], that did not teach [the case of one who] placed [his eiruv].

Rashi on Eruvin 61b:5:2.hebrew: אי נימא ר"ע - דלית ליה בהניח מהלך את כולה — אמאי תני עיר דומיא דמערה, למימר דבחריבה קאי:
Rashi on Eruvin 61b:5:2.english: If we say Rabbi Akiva - who does not hold [that] in [the case of one who] placed [an eiruv] he walks through all of it — why did [the tanna] teach "city" similar to "cave", to say that it refers to a desolate [city]?

Rashi on Eruvin 61b:5:3.hebrew: אפי' ישיבה נמי - הניח, לר"ע — לא. והא ליכא למימר: דהא דנקט חריבה משום שבת נקט, למימר: אע"ג דהיא חריבה, היכא דשבת מהלך את כולה — הא מאי איריא עיר? אפילו תל ונקע, וקמה קצורה ושיבולין מקיפות אותה, אמרן בפרקין קמא (דף טו.): מהלך את כולה:
Rashi on Eruvin 61b:5:3.english: Even [if it was] inhabited, also - [If one merely] placed [his eiruv], according to Rabbi Akiva, [he may] not [walk through all of it]. And one cannot say that the reason [the baraita] formulated [the case of] a desolate [city] was on account of [the case where one] established residence, to say that even though it is desolate, where one established residence he walks through all of it — for why specifically a city? Even [on] a mound, and [in] a cleft, and [in] standing grain that was harvested with stalks surrounding it, we said in our first chapter (daf 15a) [that] he walks through all of it.

Rashi on Eruvin 61b:5:4.hebrew: אלא לאו רבנן - ושמע מינה: בחריבה מודו; דהא על כרחך, הא דנקט חריבה — משום שיורא דשייר ולא תנא הניח נקט לה:
Rashi on Eruvin 61b:5:4.english: Rather, is it not the Rabbis? - And deduce from this that in [the case of] a desolate [city] they agree; for perforce, the fact that [the Tanna] specified a desolate [city] — he specified it on account of the omission that he omitted, [namely,] that he did not teach 'placed [an eiruv]'.

Rashi on Eruvin 61b:6:1.hebrew: אף מערה ישיבה - ולאשמועינן דאפ"ה: שבת — אין, הניח — לא — כר"ע:
Rashi on Eruvin 61b:6:1.english: So too the cave [is] inhabited - And [this comes] to teach us that even so, [if one] established his Shabbat residence [there, then] yes; [if one merely] placed [his eiruv there, then] no — in accordance with Rabbi Akiva.

Rashi on Eruvin 61b:7:1.hebrew: והא כמערת צדקיהו קתני - ואין שם דיורין [דרין], דהא של מלך היתה; א"נ, השתא לית בה דיורין:
Rashi on Eruvin 61b:7:1.english: Doesn’t [the baraita] teach: "Like the Cave of Zedekiah"? - And there are no inhabitants [dwellers] there, for it belonged to a king; alternatively, now there are no inhabitants in it.

Rashi on Eruvin 61b:8:1.hebrew: בבי כנישתא דבי אגובר - בית הכנסת גדול היה, וכולו מובלע באלפים של תחום מברכתא. והם לא היו חוששין להוליך העירוב עד סופו ולהניחו שם, דסבירא להו כרבנן: דכיון מונח באויר מחיצות, מהלכין את כולו וחוצה לו אלפים:
Rashi on Eruvin 61b:8:1.english: In the synagogue of Beit Agovar - It was a large synagogue, and all of it was encompassed within the two thousand [cubits] of the Shabbat limit of Mavrakhta. And they were not concerned with carrying the eiruv to its end and placing it there, for they held in accordance with the Rabbis: that since [the eiruv] is placed within the airspace of partitions, one may walk through all of it, and outside of it two thousand [cubits].

Rashi on Eruvin 61b:8:2.english: Go further inside it - Go deeper inside to place the eiruv all the way to its end and deposit it there.

Rashi on Eruvin 61b:8:3.english: So that more will be permitted to you - For you need to measure from the place of the eiruv.

Rashi on Eruvin 61b:9:1.english: Argumentative one - You disagree with the Sages.

Rashi on Eruvin 61b:9:2.hebrew: בעירובין לית דחש להא דר' עקיבא - דקי"ל, הלכה כדברי המיקל בעירוב:
Rashi on Eruvin 61b:9:2.english: With regard to eiruvin, nobody is concerned about this [opinion] of Rabbi Akiva - For we hold that the halakha is in accordance with the words of the one who is lenient with regard to an eiruv.

Tosafot on Eruvin 61b:11:1.hebrew: הדר. ר' אליעזר בן יעקב אומר עד שיהו ב' ישראלים אוסרים כו' - משמע דאתרוייהו קאי ר"א בן יעקב: אעכו"ם ואכותי. ובגמ' מפרש דטעמא דראב"י: דכיון דעכו"ם חשוד אשפיכות דמים, בתרי — דשכיחי דדיירי — גזרו בהו רבנן, שמא ילמד ממעשיו, כו'. וא"ת: והרי כותים, דלא חשידי אשפיכות דמים ולא ארביעה — כדמוכח פ"ק דמס' ע"ג (דף טו:), שמעמידין בהמה בפונדקאות של כותים ומתיחדין עמהם — א"כ שכיחי דדיירי, ונגזור בחד! ואין לומר דר"א בן יעקב סבר דכותים גרי אריות הן וחשידי, דהא אפילו למ"ד גרי אריות הן, לא חשידי, מדפריך התם בע"ז עלה מברייתא דאסרו למכור בהמה דקה לכותים, ורוצה להוכיח מתוך כך דטעמא משום דאתי לזבוני לעכו"ם, ולא משום דחשידי; ואמאי? דלמא בכותים: גרי אריות או גרי אמת הן — פליגי! ואומר ר"י, דעיקר תקנה משום עכו"ם איתקן, שמא ילמד ממעשיו, ולא משום צדוקי וכותי; ואגב שאסרו בעכו"ם, אסרו נמי בכותי. וכיון שלא נאסר אלא ע"י עכו"ם, לא החמיר בהן יותר מן העכו"ם:
Tosafot on Eruvin 61b:11:1.english: "One who resides." Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says: Until there are two Israelites who prohibit, etc. - This implies that Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov refers to both [cases]: to a gentile and to a Samaritan. And in the Gemara [it] explains that the reason of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov is: that since a gentile is suspected of bloodshed, [only] in [the case of] two [Jews] — who commonly reside [with him] — did the Rabbis decree concerning them, lest [a Jew] learn from his deeds, etc. And if you say: But behold, Samaritans are not suspected of bloodshed nor of bestiality, as is proven in the first chapter of Tractate Avodah Zarah (15b), for one may place an animal in the inns of Samaritans and may seclude oneself with them; if so, it is common [even for a single Jew] to reside [with them], so let us decree in [the case of] one [Jew]! And one cannot say that Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov maintains that Samaritans are lion-converts and [thus] are suspected, for even according to the one who says that they are lion-converts, they are not suspected. For [the Gemara] there in Avodah Zarah objects against this from a baraita that [the Sages] prohibited selling small livestock to Samaritans, and [the Gemara] wishes to prove from this that the reason is because he might come to sell it to a gentile, and not because they are suspected; but why [explain it that way]? Perhaps they disagree regarding Samaritans: whether they are lion-converts or true converts! And the Ri says that the primary enactment was instituted because of the gentile, lest [the Jew] learn from his deeds, and not because of a Sadducee or a Samaritan; and incidentally, when they prohibited in [the case of] a gentile, they also prohibited in [the case of] a Samaritan. And since it was prohibited only on account of the gentile, [the Sages] were not more stringent regarding them than regarding the gentile.

Tosafot on Eruvin 61b:13:1.hebrew: אמר רבן גמליאל מעשה בצדוקי א' כו' - קסבר: צדוקי אינו כעכו"ם, כדמפרש בגמ'. ופי' בקונטרס: אבל בכותי מודה דהרי הוא כעכו"ם, משום דגרי אריות הן. ואע"ג דת"ק דאסר כותי היינו רבי מאיר, כדאמר בגמ', ושמעינן ליה דקסבר גרי אמת הן בפרק ד' וה' (ב"ק דף לח:), ואפ"ה אסר בכותי — מ"מ הוצרך בקונטרס לפרש טעמא דר"ג משום גרי אריות; דת"ק ניחא, דלא מפליג בין צדוקי לכותי, ואסר צדוקי אע"ג דישראל גמור הוא, וה"ה בכותי; אבל לר"ג דמפליג בין צדוקי לכותי, ע"כ צריך לומר משום דצדוקי ישראל גמור הוא, וכותי עו"ג גמור דגרי אריות הן. ומיהו קשיא לר"י, דמשמע בהדיא בפ"ק דגיטין (דף י.) דר"ג סבר ליה דכותים גרי אמת הן, דמכשיר גט ששני עדיו כותים! ואמר נמי בפ"ק דחולין (דף ה:) דר"ג ובית דינו נמנו אשחיטת כותים ואסרוה, ומפרש התם טעמא משום דסבירא להו כר"מ דגזר על יינם לפי שנמצא להם דמות יונה וחייש למיעוט — ש"מ דגרי אמת הן, דאי גרי אריות הן לא היה צריך למיגזר עליהן, ומאליהן קמיתסרי! ובקונטרס פירש דההיא רבן גמליאל בנו של ר' יהודה הנשיא. אבל תימה, דבכל מקום רגיל לקרותו או "רבן גמליאל בר רבי" או "רבן גמליאל בנו של ר"י הנשיא"! ועוד, דלא יתכן דר"מ, דהוה קודם רבן גמליאל בר רבי, גזר על יינם דרבנן ושבק שחיטה דאורייתא, שהוצרך ר"ג ב"ר לגזור עליה! ועוד, דאין סברא כלל דאם גזר על יינם משום יין נסך שתהא שחיטתם מותרת, כיון שנחשבו כמומרי' לעכו"ם, דהא אמרינן בפ"ק דחולין (דף ה.): מומר לעכו"ם אסור לאכול משחיטתו! אלא ודאי ר"ג דיבנה הוה, ותחלה גזר על שחיטה דאורייתא ושבק סתם יינם דרבנן; ואע"ג דר"ג קודם דר' מאיר הוה, תלי אותו בדר"מ, משום דפשיטא לן בכל דוכתא דחייש ר"מ למיעוט. ולספרים נמי דגרסי הכא רשב"ג — הא שמעינן ליה בפ"ק דחולין (דף ד.) דס"ל כותים גירי אמת הן, גבי מצת כותי מותרת, דקתני: רשב"ג אומר: כל מצוה שהחזיקו בה כותים יותר מדקדקין בה מישראל! ועוד, דאם כן מה חדשו ר' אמי ור' אסי במה שעשאום עכו"ם גמורים לבטל רשות וליתן רשות? והלא כך היו מעולם לכ"ע! דליכא למימר דמעיקרא גזור ולא קבלו מינייהו, דלענין שחיטה ויין נסך הוא דקאמר התם גזור ולא קבלו מינייהו. ונראה לר"י דבין צדוקי ובין כותי לדירה אינם כעכו"ם. ומה שלא הוסיף כותי בחסורי מחסרא בגמ' "ר"ג אומר צדוקים וכותים אינם כעכו"ם", היינו משום שלא בא המתרץ אלא לתקן שלא יקשה "צדוקי מאן דכר שמיה". ועוד י"ל דאפילו ר"ג עצמו לא הזכיר בדבריו כשחלק על תנא קמא אלא צדוקי לבדו, לפי שלא הביא ראייה אלא מצדוקי. וא"ת: אי גרס רשב"ג, היכי פסקינן בגמרא כר"א בן יעקב? ור' יוחנן נמי דקאמר: "נהגו כר"א בן יעקב", הא ר' יוחנן נמי אמר: "הלכה כרשב"ג במשנתינו"? וי"ל דלא פסקינן בגמרא כר"א בן יעקב אלא על עיקר דבריו, דלא אסר בחד ישראל עד שיהו שנים; אבל בהא דסבר ליה כת"ק דכותים כעכו"ם לא פסקינן כוותיה, ואפשר דבהא הלכה כרשב"ג דאינן כעכו"ם. ועוד, דהאידנא לא נפקא לן מידי לענין כותים לבסוף כשעשאום עכו"ם גמורים:
Tosafot on Eruvin 61b:13:1.english: Rabban Gamliel said: There was an incident involving a certain Sadducee, etc. - [Rabban Gamliel] holds that a Sadducee is not like an idolater, as [the Gemara] explains in the Gemara (68b). And Rashi explained: But regarding a Samaritan, he concedes that he is like an idolater, because they are lion-converts [and not genuine proselytes]. And even though the First Tanna who prohibited [carrying in a courtyard with] a Samaritan is Rabbi Meir, as [the Gemara] states in the Gemara, and we have learned that he holds that they are genuine converts in chapter Arba'ah VeChamishah (Bava Kamma 38b), and even so he prohibited in the case of a Samaritan — nevertheless, Rashi was forced to explain Rabban Gamliel's reasoning as being because [Samaritans] are lion-converts. For [according to] the First Tanna it works out well, since he does not distinguish between a Sadducee and a Samaritan, and he prohibits in the case of a Sadducee even though he is a full Jew [by descent], and the same applies to a Samaritan; but according to Rabban Gamliel, who distinguishes between a Sadducee and a Samaritan, perforce one must say that [this distinction is] because a Sadducee is a full Jew, whereas a Samaritan is a complete idolater, as they are lion-converts. However, this is difficult to the Ri, for it implies explicitly in the first chapter of Gittin (10a) that Rabban Gamliel holds that Samaritans are genuine converts, as he validates a bill of divorce whose two witnesses are Samaritans! And it also says in the first chapter of Chullin (5b) that Rabban Gamliel and his court took a vote regarding the slaughter of Samaritans and prohibited it, and [the Gemara] explains there the reason is because they held in accordance with Rabbi Meir, who decreed against their wine because an image of a dove was found for them [on Mount Gerizim], and he was concerned for a minority [who might worship it] — learn from this that they are genuine converts, for if they were lion-converts, there would have been no need to issue a decree against them, as they would have been prohibited on their own! And in Rashi [in Chullin], he explained that that was Rabban Gamliel the son of Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi. However, this is astonishing, for in all places [the Gemara] is accustomed to call him either "Rabban Gamliel beribbi" or "Rabban Gamliel the son of Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi"! And furthermore, it is not plausible that Rabbi Meir, who preceded Rabban Gamliel beribbi, would have decreed upon their wine, which is rabbinic, yet left aside slaughter, which is Torah law, such that Rabban Gamliel beribbi had to decree upon it! And furthermore, it is not reasonable at all that if he decreed against their wine on account of libation wine, their slaughter would be permitted, since they were considered like apostates regarding idolatry; for behold, we say in the first chapter of Chullin (5a): An apostate regarding idolatry — it is prohibited to eat from his slaughter! Rather, certainly it was Rabban Gamliel of Yavneh, and he initially decreed upon slaughter, which is [governed by] Torah law, and left aside their ordinary wine, which is rabbinic; and even though Rabban Gamliel was prior to Rabbi Meir, [the Gemara in Chullin] connects it to the view of Rabbi Meir because it is obvious to us everywhere that Rabbi Meir is concerned for a minority. And even according to the manuscripts that read here "Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel," behold, we have learned that he holds in the first chapter of Chullin (4a) that Samaritans are genuine converts, regarding [the teaching]: "The matzah of a Samaritan is permitted," where it is taught: "Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: Any mitzvah that the Samaritans adopted, they are more meticulous in its observance than Jews"! And furthermore, if so, what innovation was introduced by Rabbi Ammi and Rabbi Assi when they treated them as complete idolaters regarding renouncing rights and granting rights? Behold, they would have been so all along according to everyone! For one cannot say that initially they decreed [this] and [the people] did not accept it from them, for it is only regarding slaughter and libation wine that it states there: "They decreed, but they did not accept it from them." Therefore, it appears to the Ri that both a Sadducee and a Samaritan, with respect to residence, are not like an idolater. And as for why [the Gemara] did not add "Samaritan" in the Gemara's [formulation of] the missing text (68b): "Rabban Gamliel says: Sadducees and Samaritans are not like an idolater," that is because the resolver came only to emend [the text] so that one would not raise the difficulty: "Who mentioned a Sadducee?" And furthermore, it can be said that even Rabban Gamliel himself did not mention in his statement when he disputed the First Tanna anything other than a Sadducee alone, because he cited proof only from [an incident involving] a Sadducee. And if you say: If one reads "Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel," how do we rule in the Gemara like Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov, and similarly Rabbi Yochanan who said: "The people acted in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov" — behold, Rabbi Yochanan also said: "The halakhah is in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel in our Mishnah"? And one can say that we only rule in the Gemara like Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov regarding the primary thrust of his statement, that he does not prohibit in the case of one Jew until there are two; but regarding that which he held like the First Tanna that Samaritans are like idolaters, we do not rule in accordance with him. And it is possible that in this [regard], the halakhah is in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, that they are not like idolaters. And furthermore, nowadays no practical difference emerges for us regarding Samaritans, since ultimately they treated them as complete idolaters.

Tosafot on Eruvin 61b:9:1.hebrew: לית דחש להא דר' עקיבא - דקיימא לן כדברי המיקל בעירוב, כדפי' בקונט'; ותחומין דרבנן, כדפי' בפ' מי שהוציאוהו (לעיל עירובין דף מו.):
Tosafot on Eruvin 61b:9:1.english: “Nobody is concerned about this [opinion] of Rabbi Akiva” - For we maintain in accordance with the lenient opinion in [matters of] eiruv, as explained in the Kunteres; and [the law of] techumin is rabbinic, as explained in the chapter [entitled] Mi Shehotzi’uhu (above, Eruvin 46a).
